narrative:
The model determined that you have a 28% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outcome were your credit history, your other installment plans, and the length of the loan you requested. Your credit history of critical or other existing credits was the single most influential piece of information. This history pushed the prediction toward approval because it signals that you have successfully managed past obligations. However, this positive influence was outweighed by the other two factors.

The fact that you already have an installment plan with a bank worked against you; among approved applicants this arrangement is quite rare, and the model viewed it as an additional financial burden that increases risk. Similarly, although your requested 12-month loan term is shorter than the 19-month average for approved loans, the model still interpreted the combination of amount, purpose (new car), and duration as carrying elevated risk in your specific situation.

Taken together, these elements tipped the balance toward denial. To improve your chances next time, focus on paying down your existing bank installment plan and, if possible, wait until your credit history shows even longer periods of on-time repayment. Once those areas look stronger, reapply; the model will then be more likely to view you as a good credit risk. (248 words)
